config.title: outline vs border

intro.title: outline vs border
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage to visually compare the outline and border properties on HTML elements. You will learn the core concept of how outline and border differ in terms of layout impact, styling options, and common use cases. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like border, outline, and box-sizing. By the end, you'll understand when to use each property to enhance your designs without disrupting page flow.
intro.usecase: Understanding the difference between outline and border is essential for creating accessible and polished interactive UI components. For example, when a user clicks on a form input field, browsers often apply a default blue outline to indicate focus, which is crucial for keyboard navigation and accessibility compliance. In modern dashboards and design systems, developers use subtle borders to define card or panel boundaries, while reserving outlines for temporary focus states on buttons, tabs, or search bars to avoid layout shifts. This distinction helps maintain visual consistency and prevents unintended spacing issues during user interactions.

objectives: Apply outline and border properties to HTML elements using CSS syntax
Construct visual examples that demonstrate the spatial relationship between border and outline
Configure distinct styling for border and outline to create layered visual effects
Manipulate outline-offset to control the spacing between border and outline
Implement interactive states where outline appears on focus while border maintains consistent styling
Integrate outline and border together to create accessible focus indicators
Update existing CSS rules to replace border with outline where appropriate for accessibility

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for styling
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a simple structure containing elements that we'll style with CSS. Start by creating a <div> element with the class 'container' that will hold our content.
steps.hint: Begin with the basic HTML structure. You'll need to create a <div> element and give it a class attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a basic HTML file with a container div that we can style with CSS in later steps.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a <div> element with class='container' inside the body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a <div> element with class='container' inside the body section.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a basic HTML file with a <div> element that has class='container' inside the body.

steps.title: Add a CSS file and link it to HTML
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file named 'style.css' in the same directory as your HTML file.
steps.hint: You can create a plain text file with the .css extension. The file should be empty initially.
steps.analogousExample: /* style.css - This is where CSS rules will go */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file named 'style.css' is created in your project directory.
successCriteria: The CSS file 'style.css' exists in the same folder as your HTML file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Make sure you've created a file named exactly 'style.css' in the same directory as your HTML file.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a CSS file named 'style.css' to proceed with styling.

steps.title: Create a container element for our examples
steps.instruction: Inside the existing .container div, add a new div with the class 'example-container' to hold the border and outline examples.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element with the class attribute set to 'example-container' between the opening and closing tags of the .container div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML will have a nested div with class 'example-container' inside the main container, ready to hold our styling examples.
successCriteria: A div element with class='example-container' is added inside the existing .container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element with the exact class name 'example-container' inside the .container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The example-container div isn't present. Add a <div class="example-container"> inside the existing .container div.

steps.title: Add the first element to apply border styling
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add a new div element with the class 'border-example'.
steps.hint: Add a <div> tag with class="border-example" inside the existing container div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A div with class 'border-example' is added inside the container, ready for CSS styling.
successCriteria: The HTML contains a div element with class="border-example" nested inside the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div with class='border-example' inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The element wasn't added correctly. Check that you have a <div class="border-example"> inside the container.

steps.title: Apply basic border properties to the first element
steps.instruction: In your style.css file, add CSS rules to give the .border-example element a solid border with a width of 4px, style of solid, and color of #3498db.
steps.hint: Use the border property or separate border-width, border-style, and border-color properties. For example: border: 4px solid #3498db;
steps.seedCode:
/* Add border styling for .border-example here */

/* Existing CSS (if any) */
steps.expectedOutcome: The .border-example element will have a visible blue border with the specified properties.
successCriteria: The .border-example selector has border properties with width 4px, style solid, and color #3498db.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your border has all three properties: width (4px), style (solid), and color (#3498db).
steps.feedbackWrong: The border properties aren't correctly applied. Check that you're targeting .border-example and using the correct border syntax.

steps.title: Add the second element to apply outline styling
steps.instruction: Add a second div element inside the container with the class 'outline-example' to create a target for outline styling.
steps.hint: Create a new div element with class='outline-example' inside the same container that holds the border-example element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A second div element with class 'outline-example' is added to the HTML structure, ready for outline styling.
successCriteria: The HTML contains a div element with class 'outline-example' placed inside the container element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element with exactly class='outline-example' inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The outline-example element wasn't added correctly. Check that you've created a div with class='outline-example' in the HTML structure.

steps.title: Apply basic outline properties to the second element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .outline-example class to give it an outline with a width of 4px, a solid style, and a color of #ff9900.
steps.hint: Use the outline property or the individual outline-width, outline-style, and outline-color properties. The syntax is similar to border but does not affect layout.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .outline-example element will have a visible orange outline around it, demonstrating the basic outline properties.
successCriteria: The .outline-example rule includes outline properties with a width of 4px, solid style, and color #ff9900.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your outline properties match the required values: width 4px, style solid, color #ff9900.
steps.feedbackWrong: The outline properties are not correctly applied. Make sure you're targeting the .outline-example class and using valid CSS syntax for outline.

steps.title: Add descriptive text labels to both elements
steps.instruction: Inside both .border-example and .outline-example divs, add a paragraph element with text that clearly labels each example.
steps.hint:
Add

Border

inside the border-example div and

Outline

inside the outline-example div.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both example divs will have clear text labels ('Border' and 'Outline') inside them.
successCriteria: Both .border-example and .outline-example divs contain paragraph elements with descriptive text labels.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some labels, but make sure both the border-example and outline-example divs have paragraph elements with descriptive text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The labels aren't properly added. Add paragraph elements inside both example divs with text that identifies each styling method.

steps.title: Add padding to see border vs outline behavior
steps.instruction: Add 20px of padding to both the .border-example and .outline-example elements.
steps.hint: Use the padding property with the value 20px for both CSS selectors.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both example elements will have 20px of internal spacing, making it easier to observe how border adds to the element's total size while outline does not affect dimensions.
successCriteria: Both .border-example and .outline-example selectors have padding: 20px; applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added padding to one element, but both .border-example and .outline-example need padding to properly compare their behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: The padding wasn't added correctly to both elements. Make sure to add padding: 20px; to both .border-example and .outline-example selectors.

steps.title: Add margin to separate the examples
steps.instruction: Add a margin property to both .border-example and .outline-example classes to create visual separation between them.
steps.hint: Use the margin property with a value like 20px or 1rem to add space around each example box.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both example elements will have equal margin around them, creating clear visual separation for comparison.
successCriteria: Both .border-example and .outline-example classes have a margin property with a value like 20px, 1rem, or similar.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added margin to one example, but remember to add it to both .border-example and .outline-example for consistent spacing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The margin property wasn't added correctly to both examples. Make sure both .border-example and .outline-example have a margin property with a value like 20px.
